subject: Reliability review and commercial path: premium SLO / pilot options
messages:
From: Amit Desai <amit@finvera.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outstanding latency incidents impacting Finvera - urgent

Jasmine / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. Over the past three weeks we've seen multiple latency spikes that have affected our payments UX (users abandoning checkout during peak windows). Summary attached (latency_report_aug2026.pdf) — key points: three incidents where p95 increased from ~220ms to ~1.2s during spikes, two sustained 15-30 minute tail events during heavy batch jobs. Our SREs found these correlate with cold KV-cache behavior and a recent model rollout to an int8 quantized variant.

Our renewal conversation is due next month and the leadership team is asking: what guarantee can Redwood offer if we upgrade to a premium SLO / reserved capacity tier? We need a clear remediation plan + timeline and commercial terms (pilot, uplift, and credits for the incidents).

Can we schedule a call this week? Prefering Wed 10–11 PT.

- Amit
Platform Reliability Lead, Finvera

Attachments: latency_report_aug2026.pdf
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit@finvera.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outstanding latency incidents impacting Finvera - urgent

Hi Amit — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. I'm really sorry to hear about the user impact. We take tail latency issues seriously and want to move quickly.

Short plan (high level):
- Immediate mitigations (within 48 hours): routing to last-known-stable model variant, enable aggressive prefix/KV cache warming on Finvera's busiest endpoints, temporary rate shaping for large batched jobs during peak.
- Short-term pilot (2 weeks): dedicated pool with pinned model variant + warmed KV caches to validate p95 improvement in your peak windows.
- Commercial path: canary pilot -> 90-day dedicated pilot -> contract amendment to Premium SLO (options in attached slo_proposal_finvera_v1.pdf). We can include a one-time credit for measurable incident impact; need a scope/metric agreement.

We can do Wed 10 PT. I'll bring Marissa (CS) for the runbook and Rishi (reliability PM) for the pilot design. Neha will coordinate commercial/renewal path.

Quick asks for the call:
- Can you confirm the exact endpoints and peak windows you see the failures on?
- If possible, send the last 48 hours of request traces or a sample of logs (deployment_log_snippet.txt would be perfect).

Call invite to follow.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: slo_proposal_finvera_v1.pdf
From: Amit Desai <amit@finvera.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Claudia Ramos <claudia@procure.finvera.com>, Finvera Platform Ops <platform-ops@finvera.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outstanding latency incidents impacting Finvera - urgent

Thanks Jasmine — Wed 10 PT works. For the call, here's what matters most from our side:
- We need a firm target for p95 tail behavior under our peak (we're looking for <450ms for the primary text-gen endpoints under provisioned traffic; current spikes breach 1s).
- A clear commitment on failover behavior (route to reserved capacity / compatible variant) when latency crosses thresholds.
- An approach to compensate for the business impact of the three incidents. Procurement will push for a credit and faster approval on a contract amendment.

Procurement contact (CC'd) will want cost delta and a shortened procurement timeline (our renewals team needs final terms by 2026-09-15).

See you Wednesday.

— Amit
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit@finvera.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outstanding latency incidents impacting Finvera - urgent

Amit — thanks for the specifics. On the call I'll walk through a technical remediation + SL options; high level notes here so procurement has context before the meeting:

Technical remediation summary:
- Root cause (short): KV cache cold-starts combined with a recent int8 quantized model rollout increased variance for long-tail requests. Some inference nodes saw LRU churn under batched backfills, causing bad cache hit rates.
- Mitigation (immediately): pin your mission-critical endpoints to the last-stable float16 variant (we can flip traffic in <30m) and enable proactive pre-warm for KV caches during your 11:00–13:00 ET peak window. We'll also blacklist the quantized variant from autoscaling until we've validated it in a canary.
- Pilot design: 14-day dedicated pilot (1x dedicated GPU pool, warmed caches, model pinned) with daily telemetry reports. Success criteria: p95 under peak windows reduced to <420ms for the pinned variant; error rate within historical baseline.

Commercial / SLO options:
- Option A (short-term): 90-day dedicated pilot + amendment to convert to Premium SLO on renewal. Premium SLO targets: 99.95% uptime monthly; p95 latency commitments for defined endpoints; incident credit formula for SLO breaches. Pricing uplift estimate: +18–25% depending on committed qps and model footprint.
- Option B (long-term): Reserved capacity contract with volume commit (12 months) and deeper price breaks but longer lead time to provision.

Credits and exceptions: we can propose a one-time credit tied to verified incidents (we generally scope credits to impact windows and measured user-facing errors). I'll prepare a proposed credit structure for the meeting.

Attachments: deployment_log_snippet.txt (for reference).

Talk soon — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Amit Desai <amit@finvera.com>

Appreciate the plan and the timeline. Two asks before the Wed call:
1) Procurement needs a written cost delta and the draft amendment language (simple terms: pilot period, uplift %, how credits apply) so they can start internal approvals. Claudia is copied.
2) Our CTO requested an expedited credit for the three incidents — even a partial credit will help unblock internal sign-off for a pilot.

We can confirm the endpoints and send the most recent traces by EOD today. If you can get the draft amendment by EOD Tue it would be ideal.

- Amit
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-03T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Finvera escalation — ask for pricing exception and expedited contract draft

Team — summary and next steps after the call with Finvera leadership this morning:
- Finvera is prepared to run the 14-day dedicated pilot immediately if we: (a) provide a written amendment (pilot + commercial uplift) by EOD Tue 2026-09-07, and (b) commit to an incident credit structure for the three verified outages.
- They want a firm p95 target for the pilot (we agreed to target p95 <420ms under their defined peak pattern) and daily telemetry shared.
- Procurement (Claudia) asked for a shortened approval path; she will accept a one-page amendment + SOW.

Asks for leadership/ops:
1) Pricing exception: recommend approving a temporary 20% uplift baseline for the pilot (we proposed 18–25% on the call; 20% simplifies internal approvals). If the pilot converts to a 12-month reserved contract we can revisit discounts.
2) Credit approval: recommend a capped one-time credit equivalent to 30% of August invoice for verified incident windows (requires legal sign-off).
3) Legal: prioritize a simple amendment template that binds the pilot period, success criteria, and credit mechanism.

If leadership approves the above I will finalize the amendment and send to Claudia by Tue EOD. Please reply urgently (1 business day) — procurement timeline is tight.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
